thread:
lina (eng-ml): Quick check — onboarding Mistral-3B-lite. Config lint failed in CI complaining about tokenizer field missing and weight URI mismatch after we moved weights to GCS. Anyone seen this pattern?

mike r.: I saw similar when we migrated repos. CI expects either 'weights.s3_uri' or 'weights.gcs_uri' depending on storage. Did the config.json for the model include a storage_type field?

lina (eng-ml): No, current config only has "weights": "gs://redwood-models/mistral3b-lite/weights.tar" and "tokenizer": "mistral/tokenizer". Lint output: "missing required field 'weights.storage' and tokenizer.special_tokens mismatch"

sanjay: @lina can you paste the lint snippet? The schema validator recently started enforcing explicit storage metadata to avoid ambiguous resolvers.

lina (eng-ml): Paste from CI:
```
ERROR: config-lint: model/config.json: field 'weights.storage' required when weights URI scheme is not s3.
WARNING: tokenizer: special_tokens not declared; defaults will be used which may change token ids.
```

harper: The quick fix is to add a small weights block and explicit tokenizer mapping. Example we use elsewhere: 
```json
{
  "weights": {
    "uri": "gs://redwood-models/mistral3b-lite/weights.tar",
    "storage": "gcs",
    "sha256": "<fill-in>"
  },
  "tokenizer": {
    "type": "hf",
    "name": "mistral/tokenizer",
    "special_tokens": {"bos_token": "<s>", "eos_token": "</s>"}
  }
}
```

mike r.: Also make sure to run `scripts/config-normalize.py` before pushing — it will fill in defaults and surface field deprecations. CI will still error if sha256 is missing for non-S3 URIs.

lina (eng-ml): Good call. Where do we store the sha256 for GCS artifacts? We usually only had that for S3 versions.

sanjay: We upload manifest.json alongside artifacts in the same bucket. ops-team can populate checksum. @harper can you grab the checksum and push a small update?

harper: On it. I ran a quick `gsutil hash` locally — won't trust until ops confirms but I can add placeholder "sha256" value and mark PR WIP.

ci-bot: build #2891: config-lint failure for branch 'feature/mistral-3b-lite-onboard' — see https://ci.redwood.internal/2891

lina (eng-ml): Also saw tokenizer id mismatches when serving because of default special token mapping differences between HF and our runtime. Any guardrails?

mike r.: We added a serving fallback in the runtime: if tokenizer.special_tokens missing, runtime will map a strict default but it emits a warning and increments a metric `tokenizer.defaulted_special_tokens`. That should catch regressions. But for onboarding we require explicit fields to avoid silent mismatch.

sanjay: Suggestion: add a small eval in the onboard checklist that runs `scripts/tokenizer-check.py --expected-bos "<s>" --expected-eos "</s>"` against the tokenizer artifact. That will detect id remaps early.

lina (eng-ml): I'll add the script call to the PR description and include the normalized config. Will ping once I push. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

harper: I will add the checksum and run the tokenizer check locally, then mark the PR ready for review.

mike r.: Ping me once CI is green, I'll take the review.

ci-bot: build #2892 queued: running config-normalize -> lint -> unit tests.

lina (eng-ml): Leaving notes in PR about why storage and special_tokens are explicit — helps future onboards.

sanjay: Nice. Totally worth the extra field to avoid production drift.
